description:
FILED s449s (Opus, agent S of round 7), as the deliberate residue of #563.
Both spellings are PRE-EXISTING; #563's repair does not change either.

perl's `<PATTERN>` is `glob("PATTERN")`, and glob's argument is a
WHITESPACE-SEPARATED LIST of patterns (perlfunc; PCL already models this
since #450 in `p-glob`).  Two spellings lose it, on the two different parse
paths a `<...>` run can take:

(a) SILENT WRONG, the `>` survives so PExpr's rebuild owns it:

      my @f = sort <./gd/*.t ./gd/a.t>;
      perl: three names (a.t, a.t, b.t)
      PCL : (p-glob "./gd/*.t./gd/a.t")   <- the SPACE is gone

    `Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_glob_after_block` concatenates the token CONTENTS of
    the run to rebuild the pattern, and whitespace tokens are not in the run
    it is handed, so a multi-pattern diamond silently becomes one impossible
    pattern.  The fix has to recover the source text (the tokens are still
    linked into the document, so `previous_token`/`next_token` can see the
    whitespace), or move the rebuild to the source-level repair that #563
    added.

(b) DROPS LOUDLY, the derailed path (§14c):

      my @f = sort < ./g-*.t >;
      perl: the two names
      PCL : statement dropped -- "Handle single node of unknown type"

    `Pl::Parser2::_repair_glob_pattern_cascade` requires the pattern to be ONE
    CONTIGUOUS WORD (`next if $pat =~ /[\s<]/`).  That guard is deliberate and
    is documented in the function: it is the belt to `_ends_term`'s braces, so
    that a shape where `_ends_term` is wrong about term position cannot be
    rewritten into a glob.  s449s closed the two `_ends_term` gaps it found
    (`PPI::Token::ArrayIndex`, a deref block's `}`), so the guard may be
    relaxable -- but ONLY with a fresh search for the breaking case, i.e. a
    `X < ... /re.../ ... >` one-liner where X ends a term and `_ends_term`
    says it does not.  Do not relax it without that search.

BAR: both spellings vs perl (multi-pattern, spaced-single, and the
zero-match forms); the four `_ends_term`-gap probes from #563
(`$#a<3&&$s=~/a>b/`, `${$x}<3&&$s=~/a>b/`, `time < 2 && "ab" =~ /a>b/`,
`$h{k}<3&&$s=~/a>b/`) unchanged; corpus-diff; a row beside the #563 rows in
`Pl/t/readline-ternary-01.t`, which carries a NOT-here comment naming this
task.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 7ea827a6) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- and worse than filed: the outcome depends on the text that FOLLOWS, and one outcome is a silent drop.
  A first probe agreed with perl by luck (patterns `./gd/*.t` with TWO slashes each); the guard row written for it failed, so
  the same three lines were run in three contexts:
    chdir "gx" or die;
    my @f = sort < ./g-*.t >;
    my @g = sort <./g-*.t ./g-a.t>;
    my @s = < ./g-a.t >;
    print "[@f] [@g] [@s]\n";
    perl: [./g-a.t ./g-b.t] [./g-a.t ./g-a.t ./g-b.t] [./g-a.t]
    PCL : [] [] []     exit 0, nothing on stderr -- the emission is (p-array-= @f (%p-sort-classic ... (p-readline))) and the
          @g / @s statements are GONE (not dropped: absent, so no census, no announcement)
  With the patterns `./gx/g-*.t` (two slashes) the same lines agree with perl; with more statements after them (scratch t650/d.pl)
  line 6 onward is ONE loud drop "Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ['Token::Quote::Double<"; rmdir ">', ...]".
  The four #563 `_ends_term` negatives (`$#a<3&&$s=~/a>b/`, `${$x}<3...`, `time < 2 && ...`, `$h{k}<3...`) = perl.
  Pl/t/readline-ternary-01.t's "NOT here, deliberately" comment now says it can be silent too (s543c, comment only).
LABEL: silent (subject rewritten).  Worth a corpus-diff SILENT-DROP look when it is fixed: the swallowed statements leave no
  `;; PARSE ERROR` trace.

=== s543q (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, CODE 6a1301ed) -- ROSETTA: EIGHT PROGRAMS, moved rare -> ordinary ===
The Rosetta census B found this task's family in EIGHT programs, as a WORD LIST written as a glob (`<w1 w2>` = glob("w1 w2") = the words: perlop "I/O Operators", a common golfing spelling of qw).  Two spellings, two PPI sites, two PCL outcomes:

(1) AN IMPORT LIST `use Module <name name>` -- 0473-Fibonacci-n-step-number-sequences, 0649-Inconsummate-numbers-in-base-10, 0710-Klarner-Rado-sequence, 1011-Periodic-table, 1364-Straddling-checkerboard (`use List::Util <max sum>` and the like; 0473 also `use feature <say signatures>`), 0119-Bifid-cipher (`use builtin <indexed floor>`).  LOUD: nothing is imported, the first call dies.
    use List::Util <max sum>;
    print max(3, 9, 4), " ", sum(1, 2, 3), "\n";
    perl: 9 6
    PCL : Undefined subroutine &main::max called at ... line 2.   (exit 255)
  PPI (vendored pcl branch): after the module name `<` is an OPERATOR, not a Readline --
    use List::Util <max sum>;   Word(use) Word(List::Util) Operator(<) Word(max) Word(sum) Operator(>) Structure(;)
  and PCL's rebuild (`Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_glob_after_block`, this task's (a)) concatenates the token CONTENTS without the whitespace, so the emission is `(p-use "List::Util" :import-args (p-list-ctx (p-readline 'maxsum)))` -- a READLINE of a filehandle named `maxsum`, not even a glob.

(2) A SPACED word list right after `[` -- 0316-Damm-algorithm, 0422-Exactly-three-adjacent-3-in-lists (a table of rows `[< 0 3 1 7 >], [< ... >], ...`).  LOUD: the whole statement is a drop ("Handle single node of unknown type"), so the table is never built.
    my @r = ([< 4 5 >], [< 6 7 >]);
    print "@{$r[1]}\n";
    perl: 6 7
    PCL : PCL: statement dropped at ... line 1 ... Handle single node of unknown type   (exit 255 when reached)
  PPI: after `[` a SPACED `<` is an operator, the unspaced one and the parenthesised one are right --
    my @r = ([< 4 5 >], [< 6 7 >]);   ... Structure([) Operator(<) Number(4) Number(5) Operator(>) Structure(]) ...      <- wrong
    my $r = [<4 5>];                  ... Structure([) QuoteLike::Readline(<4 5>) Structure(]) ...                       <- right
    my @r = (< 4 5 >);                ... Structure(() QuoteLike::Readline(< 4 5 >) Structure()) ...                     <- right
  (this is (b) of the s449s text: `_repair_glob_pattern_cascade` takes only one contiguous word).

A NEIGHBOUR the probes met (no program depends on it): `my %h = map { $_ => 1 } < a b >;` is SILENTLY empty (perl a,b; PCL prints an empty line, exit 0) -- the after-a-block site with a leading space (PPI: `Structure(}) Operator(<) Word(a) Word(b) Operator(>)`).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): every one of the eight programs with ONLY its `<...>` word lists spelled `qw<...>` loses this complaint (0473 0316 0422 1011 1364 become byte-identical to perl; 0649 0710 0119 then show their other causes, #5560 `\K`, a signature-sub `state` variable and `builtin::indexed`).
THE FIX NEEDS THE USER'S WORD: both sites are PPI mis-lexes (rule 13: the fix goes on the vendored branch, `docs/ppi-fix-at-source-s527.md`), and the PPI program is CLOSED (section 11 lists this task as a branch item owed to the USER).  The PCL half of (1) -- keep the whitespace when the run is rebuilt -- is a few lines in `_fix_ppi_glob_after_block` and would make spelling (1) right without a branch change (then `<max sum>` is the glob `max sum` = the two words).
frequency moved rare -> ordinary: eight Rosetta programs (the ruling: one real program is the evidence).

subject: SILENT WRONG: a diamond glob holding WHITESPACE (`sort < ./g-*.t >`, `<./a ./b>`) -- depending on the `/`s LATER in the file it globs right, DROPS loudly, or becomes `(p-readline)` and swallows the next statements with no drop announced
